Press conferences

Transcript of Chairman Warsh's Press Conference

CHAIRMAN WARSH.

Good afternoon, everyone. Inflation has eased considerably over the past year.

The labour market remains solid, with employment continuing to grow at a steady pace.

We will not hesitate to keep the federal funds rate at an appropriate level as the data evolve.

We remain attentive to developments.

We are watching inflation closely.

The risks to the economic outlook are broadly balanced.

MICHELLE SMITH.

Mr. Chairman, how confident are you about the path of inflation? Is the Committee still considering another rise in the federal funds rate this year?

CHAIRMAN WARSH.

That is an important question. We will continue to study the data carefully.

CHRIS RUGABER.

Mr. Chairman, the unemployment rate stood at 4.1 percent in June 2026. Given that, is inflation really expected to remain around 2.1 percent in 2027?

CHAIRMAN WARSH.

The unemployment rate stood at 4.1 percent in June 2026, which remains low.

Inflation is expected to average 2.1 percent in 2027.

MICHELLE SMITH.

Chairman, does the Committee see the natural rate as having risen?

CHAIRMAN WARSH.

That is a good question, and our assessment has not changed.

STEVE LIESMAN.

Chairman, markets appear to be pricing rate cuts next year. Can you walk us through the growth outlook? Is GDP really expected to grow by 3.0 percent in 2026?

CHAIRMAN WARSH.

The Committee remains patient, and we will take the incoming data into account.

GDP is expected to grow by 3.0 percent in 2026.

MICHELLE SMITH.

Do you see wage pressures continuing to build?

CHAIRMAN WARSH.

Wage growth has continued, but the pace has moderated in recent months.

KEVIN LIN.

Chairman, how would you characterize the current stance of policy?

CHAIRMAN WARSH.

Economic growth has continued at a solid pace.

VICE CHAIR DONALD LERNER.

Let me add that longer-run inflation expectations remain well anchored.

MICHELLE SMITH.

Chairman, what about the outlook for financial conditions?

CHAIRMAN WARSH.

We will consider each question on its merits as it comes before us.

RALPH AINSWORTH.

Chairman, are financial conditions still accommodative, and what risks do you see?

CHAIRMAN WARSH.

Financial conditions have tightened notably over the course of this year.

The risks to the outlook are clearly tilted to the downside.

Federal Reserve Board, 2026
